desc: Education organised as a network rather than a building — pop-up cities, microschool co-ops, online cohorts, alternative academies. The institutions that pull learning out of the 19th-century factory model and rebuild it around the people, places, and timing each learner actually needs.

label: Curation Craft
desc: The actual practice of choosing well. How a serious curator reads, watches, holds the editorial line, and protects the work against drift.

label: Aligned Goods
desc: The FRQNCY-picked tools, books, and objects across every category. Curation expressed as a department store.

label: Discernment
desc: The ability to know — quickly — what is real, what is alive, what is worth attention. Trained through practice, sharpened by the editorial bar.

label: Editorial Line
desc: What FRQNCY says yes to and what it does not. The standards that turn an aggregator into a publication.
picks: The Library of Babel — Jorge Luis Borges

label: Criticism
desc: The lineage of people who told us what was good and what was not — Ruskin, Sontag, Berger — and the craft of doing it without becoming a hater.

label: Storefronts
desc: The shopfront as a curatorial act. From the FRQNCY Aligned Goods page to a founder's first checkout flow — how to sell without selling out.

label: Marketplaces
desc: Two-sided markets where producers meet buyers. Etsy, Substack, Echo, Shopify — the operating systems of how people exchange in the new economy.

label: Affiliates
desc: Referral economics done with integrity. Recommending what you actually use, and earning when others act on it. The honest version of the kickback.

label: Membership
desc: The recurring relationship — between a network and the people it serves. How belonging is offered, priced, and held.

label: Referrals
desc: Word of mouth, structured. The mechanism FRQNCY uses to grow without paid acquisition — and to reward the people who carry it forward.

label: Donations & Tipping
desc: The voluntary half of commerce. Tipping creators, funding free work, supporting the projects that need to exist regardless of what they earn.

label: Companies
desc: FRQNCY-aligned companies — for-profit builders making products and tools that serve human flourishing. The merchants of the network.

label: DIY
desc: Do it yourself. The autonomy practice of making, fixing, building, growing — what you need with your own hands. Where dependency on systems gets quietly traded for capability.

label: Eco-Villages
desc: Intentional communities living lightly on the land — regenerative agriculture, local energy, shared infrastructure, decisions made face-to-face. The settled form of the FRQNCY ethos: people choosing to live by the values they hold.
